the-log-cabin-lady-an-anonymous-autobiog: Published anonymously through editor Marie Mattingly Meloney, this is the plain-spoken life story of a pioneer woman. From log-cabin childhood through the hard work of building a life on the frontier, she tells what settlement really cost and gave. Unadorned and deeply human, it is a precious firsthand voice from America's westward years.
the-adventure-of-living-a-subjective-aut: John St. Loe Strachey, the influential editor of The Spectator, looks back on a life at the center of British journalism and public debate. He recalls the politicians, writers, and controversies he knew, all filtered through his own strong opinions. Frank, combative, and full of insider stories, it is a vivid self-portrait of Edwardian England's press.
